semantically_equivalent_models.justification: "gpt-j" and "gpt-neox" are both implementations of transformer-based language models developed with similar architectural goals and purposes. They share many characteristics in terms of function and application.

"gpt-j-6b" and "gpt-neox" are semantically equivalent as both are specific subsets or versions of the GPT architecture designed for similar tasks, particularly with an emphasis on open-access modeling.

parent_models.justification: "gpt" is the broad and foundational model on which models like "gpt-neox" are built. It signifies the general idea and framework of Generative Pre-trained Transformers, of which "gpt-neox" is a specific iteration.

closest_parent_model.justification: As a foundational term, "gpt" represents the entire class of models that includes "gpt-neox" and most related transformer language models. It encompasses the general concepts applied in "gpt-neox".

child_models.justification: As a direct equivalent in terms of design and purpose, "gpt-j" acts as a near-child model of "gpt-neox," both being implementations of specific advanced open-access transformer architectures.
"gpt-j-6b" can be considered a specialized child model focusing on a particular framework or capability set within the broader "gpt-neox" style of language handling.

closest_child_model.justification: "gpt-j" is directly aligned with the goals and architecture style of "gpt-neox," making it the most semantically close model in terms of purpose and implementation specificity.

sibling_models.justification: "gpt-xl" is a close implementation variant focusing on expansive and high-capacity project goals similar to "gpt-neox".
Another branch of the GPT magical forest, "gpt-2" is designed under similar language model designs but distinct implementation goals.
"gpt-3" represents another sophisticated implementation of the GPT lineage with similar design but different scale and capacity lessons derived from "gpt-neox."

closest_sibling_model.justification: Due to its similarly expansive and high-capacity project goals that align closely with the design and scope of "gpt-neox," "gpt-xl" stands as the closest sibling.

unrelated_models.justification: The abbreviation "gp" is quite vague and doesn't denote any specific generative model like "gpt-neox," making it unrelated.
"gp-tsm" appears unrelated, primarily through a lack of direct connection to the specific architecture and purpose of "gpt-neox."
"pct" does not relate to GPT-based models and seems to belong to a different category of neural models.
Graph Attention Networks (GAT) are disconnected from the Transformer architecture focus of "gpt-neox."
This model does not contextually or functionally align with the language model lineage of "gpt-neox."
